commands_with_deadlines_and_results.command: go test -count=3 on the three race-prone tests

identities.suite: bounded local controls only (t.TempDir host dirs, fake clock, re-exec child helper); no live suite, no network
identities.host_profile: darwin arm64 (flock arbitration; unix-only like the P10/P11 leases)
identities.observer: ProbeLane per-lane witness (registry + fresh-open EX probe)

retained_facets: two repository roots cannot bypass the gate (same-process contention + real cross-process holder via test-binary re-exec; kernel flock alone decides across processes)
nested producer demand fails fast without deadlock (structural: nested check before any kernel call, all flock LOCK_NB, documented order; bounded-select proof)
deadline-at-success is failure (fake-clock exact boundaries: at/past fail, 1ns-before succeeds)
no case starts unless body plus cleanup fit strictly inside the budget (over/equal/fills refuse, inside admits; refusals hold nothing)
atomic declared-peak reservation (busy lane fails the whole demand naming the lane; no partial takes)
mutual exclusion under contention (2 rounds x 8 contenders, exactly 1 winner, max 1 concurrent holder, all goroutines joined)
single-shot verdicts (Complete twice reports released; Release idempotent; probe transitions held/free)

integrator_fixes: fail path now releases partial kernel takes in reverse acquisition order, matching the documented convention (close order is semantically moot for flock but the doc promised it)
doc wording: registry arbitrates identically wherever the package builds (was every platform; flock is unix-only and the package cannot build on Windows, consistent with the P10/P11 leases)
resource_and_cleanup_receipts: host lock dirs and roots in t.TempDir; child helper reaped via explicit flag (no double-wait); no strays
no repo writes outside owned P12 paths
reviewer_disposition: integrator accepted: read all 3 source files and the full test file (1149 lines); traced the registry/kernel consistency (mark-before-lock with backstop, close-before-unmark windows, same-Host in-flight nested branch, Grant.mu leaf ordering with no lock cycle); independently re-ran vet/tests/race plus a 3x contention stress. The cross-process test genuinely proves kernel arbitration (parent registry empty, refusal must come from flock). Loser-outcome tolerance (busy-or-nested) in the contention test is honest: same-Host racers behind a held/in-flight demand correctly see nested-demand, and the strict assertions (exactly 1 winner, max 1 holder) stand. Two cosmetic fixes only. Independent final review deferred to Z06.
limitations: unix-only arbitration (syscall.Flock): same platform scope as the P10/P11 leases
one Host holds at most one live Grant: multi-lane peaks must be declared atomically in one Demand (second Admit on a holding Host is nested-demand by design)
registry keys are absolute-but-symlink-unresolved paths: same-dir-different-spelling same-process contenders miss the registry fast path but still arbitrate correctly via the kernel backstop
Complete reads the clock after releasing: strictly conservative (a completion straddling the deadline reports exceeded)
a wedged child holder costs the test's 15s bound, not a hang; holder crash self-heals (OS closes fds, registry dies with the process)
